name: EBIT and EBITDA
description: Calculate EBITDA by adding depreciation and amortization back to operating profit (EBIT).
formula: EBIT = Operating Profit; EBITDA = EBIT + Depreciation & Amortization
business_contexts: a private equity firm assessing EBITDA on a target company
a manufacturer assessing EBITDA after heavy equipment depreciation
a telecom company assessing EBITDA given large network amortization
a hospital system assessing EBITDA for a lending covenant
a logistics company assessing EBITDA on a fleet-heavy balance sheet
question_patterns: Given the revenue, COGS, operating expenses, and D&A below, what is EBITDA?
Calculate EBITDA from the figures given.
What is EBITDA, given the revenue, COGS, operating expenses, and D&A shown?
Calculate EBITDA by adding D&A back to EBIT, using the figures below.
Using the figures given, what is EBITDA?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate gross profit = revenue − cogs
Step 2: Calculate EBIT (operating profit) = gross profit − operating_expenses
key_insight: EBIT is operating profit; EBITDA adds depreciation and amortization back on top, stripping out non-cash accounting charges to approximate cash operating earnings — the two are related but not interchangeable.
common_mistakes: Subtracting D&A instead of adding it back
Adding D&A to revenue instead of to EBIT
framework_soundbite: EBITDA is EBIT with D&A added back — operating profit before the non-cash charges.
